commands.review_summary:
Adds optional `title` and `toolCallId` metadata to Gateway exec approval requests/events, stores it on pending exec approvals, and updates ACP permission relay tests to consume it.

PR surface: Source +20, Tests +145. Total +165 across 8 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows current main cannot preserve `title`/`toolCallId` on structured approval events, and the PR head still does not pass those fields from the actual exec tool caller into approval registration.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] The PR needs contributor action for rebase/conflict cleanup, production metadata wiring, and real behavior proof; ClawSweeper should not queue an automated repair while the external proof gate is unmet.

target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata
target.body:
## Summary

- Back ACP structured exec approval metadata with a real Gateway request contract instead of parser-only field reads.
- Allow `exec.approval.request` to carry optional `title` and `toolCallId`, store sanitized metadata on the pending approval request, and broadcast it through `exec.approval.requested`.
- Add Gateway producer and ACP translator regression coverage, including a Gateway-produced event passed into `AcpGatewayAgent.handleGatewayEvent` and resolved through the Gateway approval handler.

## What Problem This Solves

The previous patch preserved `request.title` and `request.toolCallId` in the ACP parser, but real Gateway `exec.approval.requested` events could not produce those fields because the closed Gateway request schema rejected them and the Gateway request producer did not store or broadcast them.

That made the ACP parser change a test-only contract: ACP appeared to preserve metadata that the live Gateway event path could not send.

This update makes structured `exec.approval.requested` events the source of truth for ACP permission `title` and `toolCallId` by adding the metadata at the Gateway schema, request builder, stored payload, producer, and translator test boundaries.

## User Impact

ACP clients receiving relayed Gateway exec approvals can keep the original tool-call correlation id and user-facing approval title instead of falling back to `exec:<approvalId>` and `Command approval requested` for early structured approval events.

This keeps permission prompts easier to correlate with the originating exec tool call while leaving approval decisions, allowed options, command hydration, and fallback behavior unchanged when metadata is absent.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #79337, which introduced ACP exec approval permission relay support.
- **Gap this fills:** #79337 covered the relay contract and fallback structured approval behavior; this follow-up backs structured approval metadata with the Gateway request/event source before ACP consumes it.
- **Linked issue context:** #3257 is related approval visibility/auditability context, but this PR is a narrower Gateway-to-ACP metadata contract fix and does not claim to close #3257.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Searched open PRs for `permission-relay toolCallId title`, `exec approval metadata`, `exec.approval.requested title`, and `ACP approval metadata`; no open competing PR was found for the ACP structured exec approval metadata contract.
- #92236 is an open progress/commentary WebChat PR and does not touch ACP exec approval permission relay metadata.
- The linked issue proof prework flagged nonlocal Discord/live channel context for #3257; this PR does not claim Discord or third-party channel proof and scopes the proof to the local Gateway approval event boundary under review.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Structured Gateway exec approval events should carry and relay real `request.title` and `request.toolCallId` into ACP `session/request_permission` instead of relying on impossible parser-only fields.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree on Linux with Node/pnpm. The proof exercises the actual Gateway `exec.approval.request` handler, `ExecApprovalManager`, Gateway broadcast payload, `AcpGatewayAgent.handleGatewayEvent`, ACP `request_permission` mapping, and Gateway `exec.approval.resolve` handler.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       200 passed (200)
```

The new translator regression case starts from a Gateway-produced event, not a hand-built ACP helper payload:

```text
Gateway exec.approval.request params:
  id: approval-gateway-raw
  sessionKey: agent:main:main
  title: Run echo raw
  toolCallId: tool-raw

Observed ACP permission request:
  rawInput.approvalId: approval-gateway-raw
  toolCall.toolCallId: tool-raw
  toolCall.title: Run echo raw

Observed Gateway resolution:
  exec.approval.resolve({ id: approval-gateway-raw, decision: allow-once })
```

Additional focused helper/parser regression still passes:

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm vitest run src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed (4)
```

Type and format gates run after the fix:

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm check:test-types

pnpm tsgo:core:test and pnpm tsgo:extensions:test completed successfully.
```

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.ts src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approval.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals.ts

All matched files use the correct format.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Gateway accepts optional approval metadata, broadcasts it on the real structured `exec.approval.requested` payload, ACP uses that metadata for `request_permission`, and the selected ACP decision resolves the same Gateway approval id.
- **What was not tested:** No hosted third-party service, Discord channel, external ACP client UI, or remote CI completion is claimed here. The proof is local and targets the Gateway-to-ACP approval event boundary that the review finding identified.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause contract fix.

## Maintainer-ready details

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the Gateway-to-ACP metadata contract under review. The patch defines optional metadata at the Gateway protocol schema, carries it through the request producer, stores it on the pending approval payload, broadcasts it in the structured approval event, and verifies ACP consumption from a Gateway-produced event.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** ACP clients can correlate the permission prompt with the original exec tool call and display the intended approval title instead of a synthetic fallback, without changing approval decisions or command execution policy.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR is limited to optional `title` and `toolCallId` metadata on Gateway exec approval requests/events and ACP permission relay consumption. It does not change channel transports, Discord proof behavior, provider execution, approval policy, or command resolution.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source of truth is the structured `exec.approval.requested` payload produced from Gateway `record.request`. Because `buildRequestedApprovalEvent(record)` broadcasts that request unchanged, the contract belongs in `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema`, the host request builder, and `createExecApprovalHandlers` before ACP reads it.
- **Patch quality notes:** The diff is focused on the approval metadata contract and matching tests. The only added `.catch(reject)` is in test harness plumbing after `Promise.resolve(...)` normalizes a `void | Promise<void>` Gateway handler return; it rejects the test promise on handler failure and does not swallow production errors.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Addressed by adding optional `title` and `toolCallId` to `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` instead of keeping a parser-only mapping.
- **RF-002:** Addressed by adding after-fix proof from an actual Gateway-produced `exec.approval.requested` event passed into the ACP translator and resolved through the Gateway handler.
- **RF-003:** Addressed by extending `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` so translator-level coverage starts from the structured event shape and verifies ACP `request_permission` metadata.
- **RF-004:** Addressed by replacing helper-only proof with Gateway handler → broadcast payload → ACP translator → Gateway resolve proof.
- **RF-005:** Addressed by removing the test-only contract risk: the schema, producer, stored payload type, event broadcast, and translator coverage now agree on the optional metadata fields.
- **RF-006:** Addressed by defining the approval-boundary contract and sanitizing `title` with the existing exec approval display sanitizer before storing/broadcasting it; `toolCallId` is normalized as a non-empty optional string.
- **RF-007:** Addressed by implementing the recommended contract-backed option. Maintainer review is still expected for the public approval-boundary decision, but the branch no longer leaves the decision implicit in a parser-only patch.
- **RF-008:** Addressed by backing `src/acp/permission-relay.ts` metadata reads with a real Gateway schema/producer source.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` for the Gateway-produced event → ACP translator proof.
- **Additional target test files:** `src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` for schema/producer coverage and `src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts` for parser helper coverage.
- **Scenario locked in:** Gateway `exec.approval.request` accepts `title` and `toolCallId`, broadcasts them in `exec.approval.requested`, ACP uses those values in `request_permission`, and ACP decision resolution still targets the same Gateway approval id.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests cover the protocol schema, Gateway producer, structured event payload, ACP translator intake, and existing parser helper without launching unrelated channel transports.
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts`
- `pnpm vitest run src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:test-types`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.ts src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approval.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 other` from the parser-only contract drift review.
- **Risk explanation:** This path crosses the exec approval display/permission boundary, so user-facing strings must be schema-backed and sanitized before ACP consumes them.
- **Why acceptable:** The metadata is optional, the existing fallback behavior remains for events that omit it, `title` uses the existing exec approval display sanitizer, `toolCallId` is only accepted as a normalized non-empty string, and approval decision semantics are unchanged. Compatibility risk is limited to adding optional schema fields, availability risk is covered by preserving request registration/resolution behavior, and security-boundary risk is covered by sanitizing display text before ACP consumes it.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low-to-moderate because this adds optional metadata to a public Gateway approval request/event contract. Existing clients that omit `title` or `toolCallId` keep the current fallback behavior, and the closed schema still rejects unrelated extra fields.

The stored approval request payload gains two optional fields only; command text, command preview, command argv, approval visibility, allowed decisions, and resolution behavior are unchanged.

## What was not changed

- Did not change ACP permission option mapping or Gateway approval decision policy.
- Did not change command hydration through `exec.approval.get`.
- Did not change legacy agent approval event parsing.
- Did not add third-party channel, Discord, or hosted provider behavior.
- Did not claim remote CI or external live proof before the updated PR checks run.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `parseGatewayExecApprovalRequestEventPayload` was updated to read `request.title` and `request.toolCallId`, but the Gateway approval request schema and producer did not define or emit those fields, so real structured `exec.approval.requested` events could not satisfy the ACP parser contract.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The metadata is now introduced at the Gateway request contract and producer, stored in the pending approval payload, broadcast through the existing `buildRequestedApprovalEvent(record)` path, and then consumed by ACP. That fixes the source-of-truth event path rather than adding downstream fallback logic.
